title: Remove Duplicate Article Views by User
prompt: Your publishing platform's `article_views` table has accumulated duplicate view records when users refreshed pages multiple times in quick succession. Write a single DELETE statement that removes duplicate views for the same article by the same user, keeping only the view record with the smallest `view_id` (the earliest recorded view). A duplicate is defined as any set of rows sharing the same `article_id` and `user_id` where more than one row exists. After the DELETE, the table should contain exactly one view record per (article_id, user_id) pair—the one with the minimum view_id. Your solution must use a subquery or correlated condition to identify which rows to delete. Follow the DELETE statement with a SELECT * FROM article_views ORDER BY view_id; to confirm the result.
schema_ddl: CREATE TABLE article_views (view_id INT PRIMARY KEY, article_id INT NOT NULL, user_id INT NOT NULL, viewed_at TIMESTAMP NOT NULL, session_id VARCHAR(50));

composite_moves: delete rows where view_id is not the minimum for its group

hints: You need to identify which rows share the same article and user combination.
Use a correlated subquery in the WHERE clause that finds the minimum view_id for each (article_id, user_id) pair.

Delete rows where view_id is NOT equal to the minimum view_id for their specific (article_id, user_id) group: DELETE FROM article_views WHERE view_id NOT IN (SELECT MIN(view_id) FROM article_views GROUP BY article_id, user_id);
answer_key:
DELETE FROM article_views WHERE view_id NOT IN (SELECT MIN(view_id) FROM article_views GROUP BY article_id, user_id);
SELECT * FROM article_views ORDER BY view_id;

_meta.scenario: a publishing platform tracking article views, comments, and editor approvals
